current_disclosures.section: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry
current_disclosures.summary: Micron faces technological barriers to meeting long-term customer needs, including achieving acceptable yields for HBM with multiple chip layers, limitations on 3D stacking, improving power consumption, and shrinking product sizes at historical rates. While the company invests in R&D for technologies like EUV lithography, these new technologies add complexity, schedule risks, and may prevent recovery of R&D investments or realization of economic benefits from density increases.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks in New Product Development and AI Execution
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces intense competition and rapid technological change in the AI market, with significant risks related to developing, qualifying, and shipping new products on time. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, while uncertainty in long-term AI adoption and potential failure to achieve return on investment pose material risks. The company cannot guarantee success against competitors like Nvidia or customers developing internal solutions, and product complexity necessitates successful high-value launches to maintain average selling prices and competitive positioning.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose risks related to rapid technological change leading to shortened product life cycles and competitive disadvantages if they fail to innovate. MU highlights that competitors' success in new technology could yield cost/performance advantages, while AMD notes that failing to adapt strategy for new products can cause loss of competitive positioning and require price discounts. Both emphasize the pressure to develop and implement new technologies on time to maintain market share.

sentences.text: Additionally, rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.
If competitors are more successful at developing or implementing new product or process technology, their products could have cost or performance advantages.

For example, the AI market is subject to rapid technological change, product obsolescence, frequent new product introductions and feature enhancements, changes in end-user requirements and evolving industry trends and legal standards.

If we fail to or are delayed in identifying, developing, qualifying or shipping new products or technologies that provide value to our customers and address these new trends, or if we fail to predict which new form factors, product features preferences or requirements consumers will adopt and adapt our business accordingly, we may lose competitive positioning, which could cause us to lose market share and require us to discount the selling prices of our products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Highly competitive and evolving market conditions
comparisons.peer_summary: The markets in which AMD's products are sold are highly competitive and rapidly evolving, with intense competition expected due to rapid technological changes, new industry standards, and frequent introductions of competitive products by current or new competitors, including those who may adapt more quickly to emerging technologies.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify rapid technological change and evolving industry standards as drivers of intense competition. MU specifically cites barriers in achieving acceptable yields for HBM and 3D memory as a key technological hurdle, whereas AMD broadly describes markets as 'highly competitive and rapidly evolving' with competitors introducing products that render existing ones less competitive. Both acknowledge the risk of competitors adapting more quickly to customer requirements.

sentences.text: These barriers include achieving acceptable yields and quality for HBM products with their multiple memory chip layers, potential limitations on stacking additional 3D memory layers, increasing bits per cell (i.e., cell levels), meeting higher density requirements, developing advanced packaging solutions, improving power consumption and reliability, and delivering advanced features and higher performance.

We expect that competition will continue to be intense due to rapid technological changes, new and evolving industry standards, changing customer preferences and requirements, and frequent introductions by our competitors or new competitors of products that may provide better performance/experience or that may include additional features that render our products comparatively less competitive.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Investment Risks and AI Technology Development
comparisons.peer_summary: Significant investments in research and development carry the risk of slow or unsuccessful returns, particularly in developing advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators and XPUs; failure to timely develop these or focus on non-adopted technologies could impair competitive position and negatively impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: MU and AVGO both highlight the risk that failure to successfully develop and implement new technologies could impair competitive position and render existing technologies obsolete. MU points to specific technological barriers like HBM yields and 3D stacking, while AVGO warns that failure to develop advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators could harm competitiveness. Both acknowledge the uncertainty of R&D investments in the context of rapid technological change.

sentences.text: If competitors are more successful at developing or implementing new product or process technology, their products could have cost or performance advantages.

These barriers include achieving acceptable yields and quality for HBM products with their multiple memory chip layers, potential limitations on stacking additional 3D memory layers, increasing bits per cell (i.e., cell levels), meeting higher density requirements, developing advanced packaging solutions, improving power consumption and reliability, and delivering advanced features and higher performance.

The industries in which we compete are characterized by rapid technological change, new technological trends such as AI and cloud computing, changes in customer requirements, frequent new product introductions and enhancements, short product cycles, evolving industry standards and new delivery methods.
In order to remain competitive, we have made, and expect to continue to make, significant investments in research and development.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor Industry Cyclical Risks and AI Sustainability
comparisons.peer_summary: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical with rapid technological change and price erosion; while AI-related products have driven record revenue, this upturn may not be sustainable, and potential down-cycles could result in excess inventory, reduced profitability, and stock price declines, possibly exacerbated by the CHIPS Act.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO acknowledge the risk of declining average selling prices (ASPs) and shortened product life cycles. MU explicitly states that rapid technological change contributes to ASP declines, while AVGO identifies 'rapid price erosion' and 'short product life cycles' as characteristics of the semiconductor industry. However, AVGO places this in the context of cyclical industry downturns and supply imbalances, whereas MU frames it as a direct consequence of technological obsolescence and competitor advantages.

sentences.text: Additionally, rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.

The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical and is characterized by rapid price erosion, wide fluctuations in product supply and demand, constant and rapid technological change, evolving technical standards, evolving markets such as AI, frequent new product introductions, and short product life cycles.

Historically, such down-cycles have also been characterized by under-utilization of manufacturing capacity, changes in revenue mix and accelerated erosion of average selling prices, which can lead to reduced profitability and a decline in our stock price.

comparisons.peer_summary: Risks in developing next-generation nodes include timing delays, lower yields, and higher costs due to advanced equipment. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, larger die sizes, and supply constraints, while new nodes typically have higher depreciation and lower yields than mature nodes.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose risks associated with manufacturing yields and process technology development. MU cites 'achieving acceptable yields' for HBM and 3D memory as a key technological barrier, while INTC details risks like 'lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields' and 'failure to achieve expected performance' in next-generation nodes. Both acknowledge that manufacturing complexity and yield issues can impact product costs and competitive positioning.

sentences.text: These barriers include achieving acceptable yields and quality for HBM products with their multiple memory chip layers, potential limitations on stacking additional 3D memory layers, increasing bits per cell (i.e., cell levels), meeting higher density requirements, developing advanced packaging solutions, improving power consumption and reliability, and delivering advanced features and higher performance.

Risks inherent in the development of next-generation process technologies include production timing delays, lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields, longer manufacturing throughput times, failure to achieve expected performance, power, and area improvements, and product defects and errata (deviations from published specifications).

Lower manufacturing yields and longer manufacturing throughput times, compared to previous process nodes, can increase our product costs, adversely affect our gross margins, and contribute to manufacturing supply constraints.

comparisons.peer_summary: The development of new semiconductor products and manufacturing technologies involves risks such as forecasting challenges, defect diagnosis delays, and execution failures. Past delays in 10nm, 7nm, and 4th Gen Xeon products have allowed competitors to gain advantages, and inventory charges for Gaudi AI accelerators amounting to $922 million were recognized in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC discuss the challenges and risks of developing new semiconductor technologies. MU notes 'technological barriers to continue to meet long-term customer needs' and 'potential limitations on stacking additional 3D memory layers,' while INTC describes 'unexpected delays' due to 'complexity of interactions among steps in the manufacturing process' and 'challenges in using new materials.' Both highlight the difficulty in forecasting and executing advanced technology developments.

sentences.text: Our key semiconductor memory and storage technologies face technological barriers to continue to meet long-term customer needs.

Forecasting our progress and schedule for developing advanced nodes and other technologies is challenging, and at times we encounter unexpected delays due to the complexity of interactions among steps in the manufacturing process, challenges in using new materials or new production equipment, and other issues.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk of failing to meet evolving industry needs
comparisons.peer_summary: Failure to meet the evolving needs of the industry and markets, driven by rapid technological changes and shifting customer requirements, may adversely impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA identify rapid technological changes and evolving industry needs as key risks. MU warns that competitors developing superior technologies could create cost/performance advantages, while NVDA states that failure to meet evolving needs due to rapid changes in technology and standards may adversely impact financial results. Both emphasize the necessity of adapting to these changes to remain competitive.

sentences.text: If competitors are more successful at developing or implementing new product or process technology, their products could have cost or performance advantages.
Failure to meet the evolving needs of our industry and markets may adversely impact our financial results.
Our accelerated computing platforms experience rapid changes in technology, customer requirements, competitive products, and industry standards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Supply chain commitments and dependency risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company relies on third-party suppliers, foundries, and subcontractors for manufacturing and has entered into long-term supply and capacity commitments, often with non-cancellable terms and extended lead times (over 12 months). This dependency reduces control over quantity, quality, and schedules. Risks include the inability to reduce commitments if demand declines, paying premiums for supply, and vulnerabilities due to geopolitical tensions or natural disasters. The reliance on indirect channels further complicates supply chain visibility and execution.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA discuss dependencies on manufacturing processes and technology development. MU highlights barriers in achieving yields for complex products like HBM, while NVDA notes risks related to foundry failures to develop high-quality process technologies and transitions to smaller geometries. Although MU focuses on design/manufacturing barriers for its own products and NVDA on supply chain/foundry dependencies, both recognize that manufacturing technology execution is critical to product success.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of rapid technological change and competition
comparisons.peer_summary: Intense competition in a rapidly changing industry may lead to decreased demand for products and technologies or declining average selling prices for Qualcomm and its customers.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM disclose risks from rapid technological change leading to declining average selling prices (ASPs) and decreased demand. MU states that rapid tech change contributes to ASP declines, while QCOM warns that such change and competition could result in declining ASPs for their products or licensees. Both link technological obsolescence and competitive pressure to pricing power erosion.

sentences.text: Additionally, rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.

Our success depends in part on our ability to adapt to such change and compete effectively; and such change and competition could result in decreased demand for our products and technologies or declining average selling prices for our products or those of our customers or licensees.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks in new product area investments and R&D failure
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm's growth depends on extending technologies into new areas like automotive and IoT, but investments may not generate expected income, succeed due to patent/standard uncertainty, or yield returns due to underestimating costs, overestimating revenue, or long design cycles in regulated industries.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM highlight the risks associated with R&D investments and the uncertainty of successfully developing new technologies. MU notes that competitors' success could render MU's technologies obsolete, while QCOM warns that investments in new product areas may not generate expected income or contribute to future results. Both acknowledge the financial risk inherent in attempting to innovate in a rapidly changing landscape.

sentences.text: If competitors are more successful at developing or implementing new product or process technology, their products could have cost or performance advantages.

Our research, development and other investments in these new and expanded product areas, industries and applications, and related technologies and products, as well as in our existing technologies and products, and new technologies, may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.
